messages:
Gina Chen: heads up — customer 'BrightLoop' on Dedicated reported a sharp p95/p99 latency jump for generation calls after we onboarded the 'zephyr-3b-newseg' model earlier this morning. They're seeing timeouts and 10x tail latency for sequences > 30k tokens. Repro steps and initial logs below.

Samir Patel: thanks. any error codes from the API or just slow responses?

Gina Chen: mostly slow responses, some 504s at the client. No 5xx from the inference runtime itself — it's hanging in tokenization + first-token generation path. Example request size and payload attached in thread.

Pranav Rao: can you paste a minimal curl we can use to reproduce? also which tokenizer variant was flipped during onboarding?

Gina Chen: minimal repro:
```
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"zephyr-3b-newseg","input":"'$(python - <<'PY'
print(' '.join(['word']*40000))
PY
)'"}'
```
Note: sequences ~40k tokens (after BPE) reliably show p99 > 7s where baseline is ~600ms on previous model.

Maria Gomez: I pulled the slowtrace from the ingest node — looks like tokenization step is returning huge token counts for some inputs (token_count jumps to 80k where prior model produced 32k). The new segmentation heuristic merged fewer merges, producing more subword tokens for CJK-heavy & concatenated code blocks.

Jeff Li: that explains KV cache churn — if token_count spikes, the runtime fills KV cache much larger and evicts frequently. Memory pressure then causes increased GC and context switching. Do we have a recent deploy that touched the model tokenizer config?

Hana Yoon: deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-15T08:23:12 -> models/zephyr-3b-newseg (sha: a1b2c3) was successful :rocket:

Pranav Rao: confirmed — PR #4821 changed the BPE merge threshold and a token-break heuristic for long sequences. It passed unit tests but not long-sequence perf tests.

Samir Patel: immediate mitigation options? priority is to restore p99 to customers.

Jeff Li: short-term options: 1) route BrightLoop to the older tokenizer variant (zephyr-3b-v1-tok) by pinning model.variant in routing policy; 2) revert tokenizer change and redeploy; 3) apply a temporary tokenizer post-process that merges adjacent tokens heuristically (cheap fix). Recommend 1 + 2.

Maria Gomez: I've already started a canary rollback for that model variant on Dedicated pool A, but that takes ~12m to warm. For immediate relief we can add a routing rule to force their org_id to use zephyr-3b-v1-tok. Ops, can you apply?

Hana Yoon: ops-bot: routing change request received. Applying rule to tenant BrightLoop -> zephyr-3b-v1-tok on dedicated-pool-a. ETA 2 minutes.

ops-bot: routing rule applied successfully to tenant BrightLoop (rule_id: r-9f4d).

Gina Chen: confirmed with customer — tail latency dropped to p99 ~720ms within 90s of routing change. They reported fewer 504s.

Pranav Rao: root cause analysis notes: the new segmentation heuristic increases tokenization granularity for long sequence boundaries (intended to improve model exact-match on code snippets), but it inadvertently expanded token counts in some inputs, causing KV cache and batching heuristics to misfire. Also found a bug where the batching window didn't cap by token_count when a single request had huge token_count — the batcher attempted to combine large requests, increasing latency.

Jeff Li: follow-ups: (A) revert PR #4821 until we add long-seq perf tests (Pranav). (B) Add a batching safety cap: max_tokens_per_batch = 16384 for now (Samir). (C) Add a regression test that runs synthetic long-sequence traces across tokenizers and checks p95/p99 under load (Maria + QA). (D) Ops to keep routing rule until we confirm rollback + warmup (Hana).

Pranav Rao: I'll open a revert PR and a follow-up that includes an opt-in flag for the new heuristic plus a perf config toggle. PRs: revert -> #4850, feature -> #4851.

Maria Gomez: collecting perf graphs and sampling traces to attach to the ticket. Preliminary numbers: before change p99 0.6s, after change 7-9s for >30k tokens, with CPU and KV cache write amplification up ~4x.

Samir Patel: ops — please also increase prefix cache TTL on the ingest path to avoid repeated tokenization for identical prefixes while routing rules are in place. That will lower load.

Hana Yoon: done — prefix cache TTL increased from 30s -> 300s for dedicated-pool-a. Monitoring p95/p99 now.

Gina Chen: customer is happy for now but wants a postmortem and timeline for permanent fix. Please include troubleshooting notes and repro commands.

Pranav Rao: timeline: revert merged and deployed to canary by EOD, full rollout blocked until we add long-seq perf test and QA signoff (target: 72 hours). I'll attach the unit + perf test matrix to the PR.

Jeff Li: operational checklist for postmortem: - Confirm warmup complete for v1 tok variant - Verify KV cache memory footprint returns to baseline - Ensure batcher cap prevents multi-request coalescing of huge token requests - Add metric alert: token_count_per_request p99 > 50k -> page oncall.

Maria Gomez: saving relevant metric queries:
```
- redwood.requests.latency.p99{model:zephyr-3b-newseg,env:prod}
- redwood.kvcache.write_amplification{pool:dedicated-pool-a}
- redwood.tokenizer.tokens_per_request.p99{model:*}
```

Samir Patel: small enhancement: add a routing-fallback policy to automatically downgrade to 'compact' tokenizer variant when p95 for a tenant crosses 2s for >5m. That would auto-mitigate similar regressions. I'll draft the policy.

Hana Yoon: ops monitoring shows p99 back to baseline for BrightLoop; other tenants on same pool are still being monitored. Will escalate to SRE if any further anomalies.

Gina Chen: thanks all — I'll file the customer-facing summary and link the internal postmortem once ready. :thumbsup: 

Pranav Rao: action items assigned in the PRs, tagging reviewers. Ping me for any blockers.

Jeff Li: noted — add a load-replay job to run the new tokenizer on a sampled corpus of long-seq requests nightly until we have a perf-safe release.

ops-bot: incident note: temporary routing rule r-9f4d created and removed on 2026-03-15T08:45:50 (status: removed)

Gina Chen: closing thread for now; will reopen if BrightLoop sees regression after rollback.
